findings.message: `experimental.agentUpgrade: "security"` is Next.js 16.4.6's default (`next/dist/server/config-shared.js:192`), so this line changes nothing. The comment is also wrong. Next.js does not record a finished agent-run upgrade with this setting. It is the policy for nudging coding agents about future upgrades (`config-shared.d.ts:366`: "Nudge coding agents about security upgrades, stable releases, or Future Defaults"; `lib/upgrade/nudge.js` reads it on each `next dev` or `build`). Delete the key and its comment. If the team wants this policy written down on purpose, keep the key and change the comment to say it sets the agent-nudge policy, not that it records the 16.4.2 → 16.4.6 upgrade.
findings.scenario: Remove `agentUpgrade: "security"` → the resolved config still has `experimental.agentUpgrade === "security"` and the nudge works the same. A reader who trusts the comment thinks it is a record of the upgrade and may keep it or edit it for the wrong reason.
